source_text: Euangelica praecepta, fratres dilectissimi, nihil sunt aliud quam magisteria diuina, fundamenta aedificandae spei, firmamenta conroborandae fidei, nutrimenta fouendi cordis, gubernacula dirigendi itineris, praesidia obtinendae salutis, quae dum docibiles credentium mentes in terris instruunt, ad caelestia regna perducunt. multa et per prophetas seruos suos dici Deus uoluit et audiri: sed quanto maiora sunt quae filius loquitur, quae Dei sermo qui in prophetis fuit propria uoce testatur non iam mandans ut paretur uenienti uia sed ipse ueniens et uiam nobis aperiens et ostendens, ut qui in tenebris mortis errantes inprouidi et caeci prius fuimus luce gratiae luminati iter uitae duce et rectore Domino teneremus.
thought_title: The gospel commands as divine teaching leading to heaven
orientation: Cyprian opens the treatise by addressing his fellow Christians and describing the gospel commands as God's teaching that guides believers from earth to heaven.
pass_a_gloss: The gospel precepts, brothers most beloved, nothing are other than divine teachings, foundations of hope to be built, supports of faith to be strengthened, nourishments of heart to be warmed, rudders of journey to be directed, protections of salvation to be obtained, which while teachable minds of believers on earth they instruct, to heavenly kingdoms they lead. Many things and through prophets his servants to be said God willed and to be heard: but how much greater are the things which the Son speaks, which the Word of God who in the prophets was with his own voice testifies, no longer commanding that be prepared for the one coming a way but himself coming and the way for us opening and showing, so that we who in darkness of death wandering unheeding and blind before were, by the light of grace enlightened, the way of life with leader and guide the Lord we might hold.

choices.why: Keeps the plural force of magisteria as concrete acts or instances of teaching, matching the series of plural nouns that follow.

choices.english: foundations of hope to be built
choices.why: Preserves the gerundive force (aedificandae) showing purpose or necessity, and keeps the genitive spei as the object of the building.
rejected: foundations of the hope that is to be built

choices.english: rudders of the journey to be directed
choices.why: Gubernacula is literally rudders or steering oars, and the gerundive dirigendi keeps the sense that the journey is what is being steered.
rejected: helms of the path to be steered

choices.why: Inprouidi means lacking foresight or improvident, not merely careless; keeping both adjectives preserves the double description of the pre-conversion state.

choices.english: having been enlightened by the light of grace
choices.why: Luminati is a passive participle, so the English keeps the passive sense of having received enlightenment, and luce gratiae is rendered as the instrument.
rejected: illumined with the light of grace

choices.english: with the Lord as guide and director
choices.why: The ablative absolute construction is rendered with 'with...as' to show the Lord is both dux and rector, preserving both nouns.
rejected: with the Lord guiding and ruling
under the Lord as leader and ruler

pass_b_english: The gospel precepts, dearly beloved brothers, are nothing other than divine teachings: foundations of hope to be built, supports of faith to be strengthened, nourishment of the heart to be cherished, rudders of the journey to be directed, protections of salvation to be obtained. While they instruct the teachable minds of believers on earth, they lead them through to the heavenly kingdom. God willed that many things be said and heard through the prophets his servants, but how much greater are the things the Son speaks, which the Word of God who was in the prophets testifies with his own voice—no longer commanding that a way be prepared for one who is coming, but himself coming and opening the way for us and showing it, so that we who previously wandered improvident and blind in the darkness of death, having been enlightened by the light of grace, might hold to the path of life with the Lord as guide and director.

last_rejected.quote: they lead them through to the heavenly kingdom
last_rejected.why: "perducunt" means "lead through to completion," but "through" here misleadingly suggests passage rather than arrival/escort.
last_rejected.fix: they lead them all the way to the heavenly kingdom
last_rejected.ruling: 'perducunt' means lead/escort to destination; 'through' is awkward but not meaning-changing.

last_rejected.quote: no longer commanding that a way be prepared for one who is coming
last_rejected.source_quote: non iam mandans ut paretur uenienti uia
last_rejected.why: "uenienti" is dative (for the coming one), but "one who is coming" misses that this alludes to preparing the Lord's way (Isaiah/Malachi), a specific messianic reference.
last_rejected.fix: no longer commanding that a way be prepared for him who comes
last_rejected.ruling: 'uenienti' = 'the coming one'; translation captures meaning. Allusion recognition is preference, not error.
